record.paper_title: Open problems in the theory of completely positive and copositive matrices
record.original_question: Let A be a real symmetric entrywise nonnegative n x n matrix, and let G(A) be the graph with vertices 1,...,n and an edge between i and j exactly when i != j and a_ij != 0. Which additional checkable conditions, whether depending on G(A) or not depending on G(A), can be found to determine or certify complete positivity of A, where complete positivity means A = B B^T for some entrywise nonnegative matrix B?

evidence.quote: It would be interesting to obtain additional, graph dependent or not, conditions for complete positivity.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $A$ be a real symmetric $n \times n$ matrix with nonnegative entries. Define the graph $G(A)$ on the vertex set $\{1, 2, \ldots, n\}$ in which $\{i,j\}$ is an edge precisely when $i \neq j$ and $a_{ij} \neq 0$. The matrix $A$ is called completely positive if there exists an entrywise nonnegative (not necessarily square) matrix $B$ such that $A = BB^{T}$.

Find additional checkable conditions—either depending on the graph $G(A)$ or independent of it—that determine, or at least certify, the complete positivity of $A$. More precisely, identify nontrivial sufficient conditions (or necessary and sufficient conditions valid on suitable subclasses of nonnegative symmetric matrices) for $A = BB^{T}$ with $B \geq 0$ entrywise, going beyond the currently known criteria such as diagonal dominance, positive semidefiniteness of the comparison matrix, or the characterization that every doubly nonnegative realization of $G$ is completely positive iff $G$ contains no odd cycle of length $\geq 5$.
artifact.status_search_result: The general problem of finding practical checkable conditions characterizing complete positivity remains open. Deciding complete positivity is known to be NP-hard, and while several sufficient conditions are known (diagonal dominance, comparison matrix PSD, graph-based criteria via no odd cycle of length ≥ 5), no complete checkable characterization is known. Recent work continues to propose new sufficient conditions but does not resolve the general question.

status_evidence.title: Copositivity and Complete Positivity (survey)
status_evidence.snippet: Checking whether a given matrix is completely positive is NP-hard; characterizing complete positivity in general remains an open challenge.
status_evidence.claim: Determining complete positivity in general is NP-hard and lacks a fully checkable characterization.

status_evidence.title: Completely Positive Matrix — Wolfram MathWorld
status_evidence.snippet: Various sufficient conditions and graph-theoretic criteria are listed, but a general checkable characterization is not given.
status_evidence.claim: Standard references list partial sufficient conditions, indicating no general checkable criterion is known.
